messages:
maya: Quick FYI — spotted public PoC for CVE-2026-0815 (libkms-client). Looks like exploit is focused on transitive deps that touch KMS calls. We should decide patch prioritization and scheduling.

dan: reading the advisory now. CVSS 7.2, remote exploit path requires credentialed access in most cases, but service brokers could expose it. Impact on Dedicated & Private higher.

alisha: Agree. We should treat Dedicated customers as high priority since they have reserved capacity + stricter SLAs. Also need to consider RBAC migration we planned — might complicate rollout.

ryan: From infra: minimal code change in libkms-client, single-line fix in token handling. Build/install should be 10–15m per image. Main risk is rolling across pools causing brief connection errors.

ops-luke: Suggest staggered roll: non-prod -> low-tier hosted -> dedicated small pools -> enterprise/private. Canary in a single region first. Window: pick 02:00 UTC for minimal impact.

maya: Timeline proposal: Tuesday 02:00 UTC canary (us-west-2), Wednesday 02:00 UTC hosted low-tier, Thursday 02:00 UTC Dedicated batch 1, Friday private customers (coordinate with account teams). Any objections?

product-marco: We need comms to customers two business days before their window. Also add automatic fallback policy: if KV-store disconnects, route to secondary region. Can we guarantee that?

ryan: We have a graceful fallback in router but it increases latency. We'll add a temporary rate-limit bump to avoid cascade. Ops runbook will include rollback commands.

maya: Runbook snippet I'll add:

```
# rollback if errors > 5% for 5m
kubectl apply -f deployment-old.yaml
route-control rollback --policy previous
notify #eng-oncall
```

alisha: Two security items: 1) Ensure audit logging captures both pre- and post-patch key usage for 30 days. 2) KMS key rotation isn't required for the fix, but customers on managed KMS should be informed.

security-bot: (automated) CVE-2026-0815 assigned to eng-security; severity HIGH; suggested score 7.2. Tracking ticket: SEC-2026-482.

dan: SLA impact: Hosted low-tier customers — negligible if canary stable. Dedicated customers: potential blips that may count as transient errors under SLA; add a 1-hour maintenance window to avoid violations.

ops-luke: Agree on maintenance windows for Dedicated. We can mark region-specific maintenance to prevent global SLA hits. We'll coordinate with SRE on alert thresholds.

product-marco: I'll draft the customer notice and post to status.redwood.ai. Include escalation contacts for private deployments.

maya: Decision summary: proceed with Tuesday canary, staggered rollout through Friday; Dedicated get maintenance windows and 2-day customer notice; audit logging extended 30d; RBAC migration won't be touched in this patch; KMS rotation optional but communicate. Action owners: ryan (build + canary), ops-luke (runbook + rollback), marco (customer comms), alisha (audit verification), dan (SLA sign-off). Anyone else to add?

deploy-bot: (deploy) Canary image build queued by ryan — image: rwd/libkms:patch-0815-rc1

ryan: I'll post canary health metrics in #eng-sre after the first 10 minutes. If healthy, we push to low-tier hosted.

maya: Thanks all. If anything changes ping @maya and escalate to incident channel. :thumbsup:"
